hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was rolled from off to on at 23:22, and the code path it enables divides by zero: the account page began failing with ZeroDivisionError in the same minute the flag flipped, and error rate jumped from ~0.5% to 25-36% and stayed there. Argus's 'set off' at 23:29:44 apparently did not take effect on serving instances (logs still show monthly-spend-feature=on through 23:29), so lack of recovery does not exonerate the flag - the toggle likely needs to be re-applied/forced and caches or the rollout ramp checked.
supporting_evidence: 2026-09-01T23:22:00Z ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
2026-09-01T23:29:00Z INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations (still 'on' after the 23:29:44 disable attempt)
Pre-onset errors are a different, low-rate failure mode: "UpstreamTimeout: payment authorization timed out" at 0-2% per minute

hypotheses.summary: Alternative: the ZeroDivisionError is latent in code that the flag only exposes, and the real trigger is data/state (e.g. a month-boundary spend total of zero) reached at 23:22 while the flag ramp coincided. In that case turning the flag off would only help if the flag actually propagated, and the fix is the divide-by-zero guard itself.

A code change (deployment) introducing the divide-by-zero is not supported: no recorded change to kukibuki-service exists anywhere in the lookback, so this ranks last and would require a deploy/release record outside the change channel to confirm.
supporting_evidence: Every recorded change to kukibuki-service from 2026-08-25T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-01T23:30:00Z. (nothing changed in this window)
